_comment: Issues #389 and #390 (F-TEST-003): reviewed DNS, TLS, QUIC, HTTP/2, S1AP, NGAP and NAS accuracy cases plus unknown/malformed traffic; issue #527: a positive and a negative case per default-chain classifier (see coverage-pending.txt for the ones still owed).
Checked by tools/ci/tests/check-accuracy-corpus.py; NOT part of ci/golden_pcaps.txt,
so the golden classification fingerprint's input set is unchanged.
expected counts are per packet: wire = carries the family's wire-protocol label,
other = attributed to a different application protocol, abstain = no application verdict;
attribution = application names the SDK derives heuristically beneath the wire label.
abstain counts include payload-less packets (e.g. TCP SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK), which carry no application data.

The 'unknown' family is the abstention family: no wire labels, cases of kind 'unknown' whose expected block states explicitly how many packets must get no application verdict (abstain) and which are still attributed (other).
SCTP chunk layers (sctp_data, ...) count as transport; a family wire label beneath another (nas_5g beneath ngap) is encapsulation, not attribution.

classifiers (optional, per case) names the mmt_check_* functions of the default TCP/UDP chains (src/mmt_tcpip/lib/inter_proto_classif_list.def) the case exercises; every chain classifier needs a positive and a negative/ambiguous case naming it, or an entry in coverage-pending.txt (issue #527).
